MEMORANDUM — DOCKETING STANDARDS (SIMULATED JURISDICTION)

Re: Computing every litigation deadline under SRCP 6 (this firm's controlling method)

I. The counting method. (a) Exclude the trigger day: the day of the event that starts the period is never counted. (b) Count every calendar day thereafter, including intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and court holidays. (c) Rollover: if the last day of the period lands on a Saturday, Sunday, or court holiday, the period runs to the next day that is not a weekend day or court holiday. (d) Service adjustment: when a deadline runs from SERVICE (not filing) and service was made by mail, add 3 calendar days AFTER the period would otherwise expire; apply the rollover rule of (c) after adding the 3 days, not before.

II. Court holidays in this jurisdiction for 2026 (exhaustive list for computation): January 1 (New Year), January 19 (Civil Rights Day), May 25 (Memorial Day), July 3 (observed Independence Day), September 7 (Labor Day), November 26 (Thanksgiving), December 25 (Christmas).

III. Periods that matter here. (1) Answer to a complaint: 21 days after service of the summons and complaint. (2) Opposition to a motion: 14 days after the motion is FILED. (3) Reply in support of a motion: 7 days after the opposition is filed. (4) Notice of appeal: 30 days after entry of judgment. (5) Rule 68-style offer of judgment: acceptance within 14 days after service of the offer.

IV. Weekday calendar anchors for 2026 (verified): June 1 is a Monday; July 1 is a Wednesday; August 1 is a Saturday; September 1 is a Tuesday; October 1 is a Thursday.

V. Firm rule. Every computed date is recorded in the deadlines register as a review record whose outcome field contains ONLY the final date in YYYY-MM-DD form. A computation that ignores the rollover rule or the mail-service adjustment is a docketing error chargeable to the responsible attorney.

This memo controls over any older docketing chart. The superseded 2024 chart (which used a count-the-trigger-day method and a 5-day mail adjustment) must not be used.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — Consolidated Rules Memo: Computing Time Under the Simulated Rules of Civil Procedure (SRCP 6)

AFFIDAVIT OF SERVICE (SIMULATED)

Case: Meridian Grain Cooperative v. Talvern Logistics Group, No. 26-CV-01847 (Simulated Superior Court).

I, Dana Whitfield, process server, being duly sworn, state: on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, at 10:42 a.m., I personally delivered the summons and complaint in the above-captioned action to Talvern Logistics Group by handing true copies to its registered agent for service, R. Calloway, at 1120 Harbor Line Road, Suite 400. Service was completed by PERSONAL DELIVERY; no mail service was used for the summons and complaint.

The defendant's answer period therefore runs from the June 3, 2026 service date under SRCP 6. Filed with the clerk June 4, 2026.

Sworn before Notary J. Ellery, commission 88-1042. This affidavit is the operative proof of service; an earlier draft affidavit misstating the date as June 1 was withdrawn and never filed.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — Affidavit of Service: Meridian Grain complaint served by personal delivery June 3, 2026

CERTIFICATE OF FILING AND SERVICE (SIMULATED)

Case No. 26-CV-01847. On Friday, August 14, 2026, Talvern Logistics Group FILED its Motion to Dismiss Counts II and IV with the clerk via the electronic filing system (accepted 3:17 p.m., confirmation EF-26-55812). Under the Consolidated Rules Memo, the opposition period for Meridian Grain runs 14 days from this FILING date — the filing date, not the service date, controls oppositions.

Courtesy service on opposing counsel was completed the same day by electronic means. No mail-service adjustment applies to deadlines measured from filing.

Docketing note: associates have twice mis-calendared motions in this matter by running the 14 days from the service email (August 17) rather than the filing date; the register must reflect the filing-date computation.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — Certificate of Service: Talvern motion to dismiss filed August 14, 2026

dm_documents.author: migration:deadline-computation
dm_documents.body:
PROOF OF SERVICE BY MAIL (SIMULATED)

Case No. 26-CV-01847. On Friday, September 18, 2026, Talvern Logistics Group served on Meridian Grain Cooperative, BY FIRST-CLASS MAIL ONLY, an Offer of Judgment in the amount of $1,450,000 inclusive of costs, deposited with postage prepaid at the Harborview station.

Under the Consolidated Rules Memo the offer may be accepted within 14 days after service; because service was made BY MAIL, the 3-day mail adjustment of SRCP 6(d) applies AFTER the 14-day period is computed, and the weekend/holiday rollover applies after the mail days are added.

No electronic service of the offer was made. The register entry for the acceptance deadline is the controlling calendar date for the client's decision meeting.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — Proof of Mailing: Rule 68-style Offer of Judgment served by mail September 18, 2026

dm_documents.author: migration:deadline-computation
dm_documents.body:
CLERK'S NOTICE OF ENTRY OF JUDGMENT (SIMULATED)

Case No. 26-CV-01847. Judgment on the verdict was ENTERED on the docket on Friday, November 20, 2026. Under the Consolidated Rules Memo, any notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days after entry of judgment, computed by the SRCP 6 method (exclude the entry day; count all calendar days; roll forward from a weekend or court holiday to the next court day; note the Thanksgiving holiday of November 26 and the Christmas holiday of December 25 fall within the period).

This notice is the operative trigger document. The earlier minute order of November 17 announcing the verdict did NOT enter judgment and does not start the appeal period.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — Clerk's Notice: Entry of Judgment November 20, 2026

2024 DOCKETING QUICK CHART — WITHDRAWN, RETAINED FOR ARCHIVE ONLY

This chart was withdrawn firm-wide after the docketing audit. It used the OLD counting method: count the trigger day as day one, apply a 5-day mail adjustment before rollover, and treat only January 1, July 4, and December 25 as court holidays. Example rows (WRONG under current SRCP 6): answer to complaint served June 3 → 'June 23'; opposition to motion filed August 14 → 'August 27'; offer of judgment served by mail September 18 → 'October 7'; notice of appeal from November 20 judgment → 'December 19'.

Every date in this chart is superseded by the Consolidated Rules Memo. Associates found relying on this chart are subject to remedial docketing training.
dm_documents.name: Deadline pack — SUPERSEDED 2024 Docketing Chart (do not use)
